a video scene can consistently be classified into identifiable classes, that the video quality, measured by MSE, can be related to certain parameters of video partitioning, and that the video partitioning parameters can be tailored to the specific characteristics, embodied by the video scene class, and the video quality, to improve the video quality.
a scene adaptive mechanism for video encoding can be achieved by classifying a video sequence into different scene types and tailoring the video encoding parameters to the scene types.
the video quality can be predicted by the parameters used in video coding and that the parameters can be tailored to the video scene characteristics to improve the video quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of adaptability in video partitioning in order to achieve better compression performance.

the development of a new video partitioning algorithm, which is adaptive to the characteristics of video scene and the video quality, and is suitable for the application of video transcoding and video storage.

the following: (i) The identification of video scene classes, (ii) The relationship between video quality and video partitioning parameters and (iii) An adaptive mechanism for the selection of video partitioning parameters, in order to achieve a good tradeoff between the video quality and the computational complexity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed scene-adaptive transform domain partitioning algorithm has a better overall performance than the conventional transform domain partitioning scheme, and that this performance is further enhanced by tailoring the partitioning parameters to the specific characteristics, as embodied in a scene class and a video quality measure, of the video scene.
, the proposed scene-adaptive transform domain partitioning mechanism is a viable approach for improving video quality in the presence of channel errors.

the proposed adaptive video partitioning mechanism is able to achieve the following: (a) a reduction of the number of motion vectors (MVs) required to represent a video sequence, (b) improved coding efficiency, and (c) improved subjective quality of the decoded video sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the video partitioning parameters can be adapted to different video scenes and that this leads to better performance in the video codec.
the proposed video partitioning scheme is adaptive to video scenes in a consistent manner, which is a significant improvement over the previous work.

the proposed adaptive mechanism is capable of providing an effective means for video scene partitioning, which is able to improve the performance of a video coding scheme, such as the H.263 standard, in terms of the coding efficiency, and the computational complexity of the video coding algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a video scene can consistently be classified into identifiable scene classes, and that this classification can be used to adaptively tune the video partitioning parameters.
video partitioning is a function of the scene complexity and the video quality and that these can be quantified and used for tailoring the video partitioning process to the specific scene.
the transform domain video partition algorithm can be made more robust to the effects of motion and activity by tailoring the algorithm to the specific video scene.
